blocks.h2: What 2013 Taught Elmhurst About Sump Pumps
blocks.body: In April 2013, more than 7 inches of rain fell on Elmhurst, and homes old and new in every part of town took on water. In a storm like that, sump pumps run for hours. Some fail from the strain, and others stop when the power goes out. A pump in good condition, sized for the pit, with a battery backup and a high-water alarm, is the setup that holds up in a storm like that.

blocks.h2: Why the Sump Pit Matters Too
blocks.body: A good pump can still struggle in a bad pit. If the pit is too small, the pump turns on and off constantly and wears out early. If it's unlined, silt can clog the pump. A cracked or missing lid lets debris in and moisture out. When we replace a pump, we look at the pit too, and recommend a new liner or lid if it will help the pump last.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: Do I need a battery backup sump pump?
items.preview: If the basement is finished, yes.
items.answer: If your basement is finished or holds anything important, yes.

items.q: How long do sump pumps last?
Can you install a sump pump in a basement without one?
items.answer: Often. We cut a new pit where water collects and run the discharge outside.

items.q: Can my sump pump discharge into the sewer?
items.answer: No. Sump water should go outside, not into the sanitary sewer.

items.q: Should I have two pumps in the pit?
items.preview: A primary and a backup is best.
items.answer: A primary pump plus a battery backup is the most reliable setup.

items.preview: A sensor that warns you when the pit fills.
items.answer: A small sensor in the pit that sounds an alarm or alerts your phone when water rises too high.

items.q: How much does sump pump installation cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on the pump, pit and backup. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, whether a pit is needed and whether you add a backup. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
